symptom: verify (and lint --baseline) passed a project whose lint rules had not run, with their findings counted as fixed: a CI checkout or worktree without .claude/lint-rules/ reported 115 findings as fixed and stopped guarding against those rules (ako/mxcli#2455); a rule that ran into an error (MPR017 'could not run', ako/mxcli#2454) was counted as a new finding and its real baseline findings as fixed, so the first verify after a change was wrong in both directions.
cause: A lint baseline stored findings only. Baseline.Compare computed Fixed as total minus matched, so any baseline finding the run did not report was 'fixed', whatever the reason: the finding was resolved, or the rule that produces it was not installed, disabled, or failed. The rule set and the configuration that produced the findings were not recorded, so a run could not tell them apart. A rule failure was also kept in the 'new' list (isNew = RuleFailure), so it counted as a finding about the project.
file: `mdl/linter/baseline.go` (BaselineMeta, WriteBaselineWith, CompareRun, BaselineComparison.Incomplete), `mdl/linter/linter.go` (RulesRun), `mdl/linter/config.go` (Config.Fingerprint), `mdl/linter/output.go` (BaselineReport in the JSON), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_lint.go`, `cmd/mxcli/cmd_verify.go` (incomplete(), Outcome.Incomplete in verify.Run).
insight: A comparison against a recorded baseline must know what the run was capable of seeing, not only what it saw: absence of a finding means 'fixed' only when the thing that would report it ran under the same configuration. The baseline now records the rules that ran and a fingerprint of the parsed configuration (from the values, so a comment or reordering does not change it), and the comparison separates fixed from not checked. The discriminating run was the one the issue gave: the same unchanged project against the same baseline with and without the custom rules directory, which went from '0 new, 3 already known, 60 fixed' to '60 not checked' and an error in verify. A rule that could not run must stay out of the findings and be reported as a fact about the run; a gate that reads 'nothing new' from a run that checked less is the same shape as a test that only passes against code that never had the fix. Left open: the annotations file `report security` reads is not consulted by verify. Found by the owner's test run of the first version: a fix that reports 'a rule did not run' must not let the very next step it recommends (--update-baseline) record that state as the new truth, so --update-baseline now refuses while a rule cannot run; and advice has to follow the cause (a built-in rule that failed needs a second attempt, not an installed rule set).
